gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-quicksand: Conthrax stretches its lowercase a wide and makes its small letters so tall the capitals barely rise above them, a geometric heading with a single-thread feel. Quicksand follows in round, glassy bowls.
gen-dafont-cowboys-fs-synonym: Cowboys leaves big gaps between its stems, each letter traced in a thin line like laser etching. Synonym adds dependable, open curves.
gen-dafont-cowboys-plus-jakarta-sans: Wide gaps between stems give Cowboys a rustic, authoritative look, as if each letter were etched with a laser. Plus Jakarta Sans keeps its curve endings well apart, so a long page moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-alpino: Disorder draws raw, chaotic letters with no swelling where curves meet stems, and its tall lowercase looks oversized. Alpino sits beneath it, cozy and tightly spaced.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-hind: Disorder looks raw and chaotic, its glyphs set well apart and its curves meeting stems without any swelling. Hind steps in with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-nunito: Nunito brings big round lowercase bowls and terminals that finish well clear of the stem, a friendly sans-serif. Disorder above it stays jagged, with diagonals as heavy as its stems.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Chaotic is the first word for Disorder, whose glyphs sit far apart and whose tall lowercase looks huge on the line. Pilcrow Rounded is a warm sans-serif with big counters; shrink the heading and that tension fades.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-quicksand: Quicksand has tall, glassy lowercase bowls and terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Make Disorder small and its raw spacing loses bite beside it.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase nearly level with the capitals, every stroke as steady as a drawn string. Early GameBoy has more thick-thin variation, so Hind reads smoothly after it.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-nunito: Playful is Early GameBoy's mood, with open tracking and a skyward x-height line. Nunito does the quiet work, its big round bowls and clear terminals easing along the plain sans text.
